memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head. Slaughter it, take some of its blood and put it on the lobes of the right ears of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Then splash blood against the sides of the altar." - Exodus 29:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Blood is applied to three specific places: the ear, the thumb, and the toe. These were not random. The ear that would hear God's word, the hand that would do God's work, the foot that would walk in God's ways — each was marked, claimed, consecrated for service.

What a picture of whole-life dedication. God was not content to claim Aaron's religious duties while leaving his listening, his working, and his walking untouched. Every faculty was set apart. There was no compartment left unclaimed by the God he served.

The same claim rests on us. Paul says we are not our own; we were bought at a price, and we should therefore honour God with our bodies (1 Cor 6:19-20). What you listen to, what your hands do, where your feet carry you — these all belong to Him. Ask yourself honestly: is my ear tuned to God's voice or to other voices? Are my hands doing work I could offer to Him? Are my feet walking somewhere He would go with me? Blood on the ear, thumb, and toe means nothing is exempt.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What am I listening to, and does it help or hinder my walk with God?
Are my hands and feet engaged in things I could genuinely offer to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You claim all of me — my listening, my working, my walking. Set apart every part of my life for Your service, and let nothing remain outside Your rule. Amen.
